subject: Sensitive-field redaction & contractual no-train: evidence and workflow
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medsys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Privacy Team <privacy@medsys.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sensitive-field redaction + contractual no-train — initial questions

Hi Sofia / Karthik,

Thanks for taking a look at MedSys' data handling needs. We’re finalizing requirements for our LLM-enabled triage workflow and have two hard constraints from InfoSec and legal: 1) certain fields (e.g., patient_id, full_name, MRN, SSN) must be redacted prior to any storage or processing that could be used for model training; 2) we need a contractual "no model training" commitment for any data that flows from our systems unless explicit, documented opt-in occurs.

Could you explain how Redwood would implement (and demonstrate) a flow that ensures these fields are never used for model improvement across Hosted and Dedicated deployments? We also need an evidence bundle we can attach to our vendor risk questionnaire — things like retention logs, a subprocessor list, and an example audit extract.

Attached: PII-redaction-spec.docx (high level list of fields & examples).

Primary asks:
- Technical approach to per-customer field redaction + proof that redaction prevents training use
- Suggested DPA amendment language for an explicit no-train clause and prompt/response ownership
- Timeline for getting a draft amendment + evidence artifacts to us

Appreciate a concise plan — legal is on a tight cycle.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Privacy, MedSys Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medsys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sensitive-field redaction + contractual no-train — initial questions

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the spec; that helps. High level response below, followed by proposed next steps. Attaching a concise explainer of our redaction approach.

Summary approach (short):
- Ingestion redaction: configurable pre-processing pipeline that strips/normalizes listed sensitive fields at the ingestion boundary for the customer namespace. The pipeline operates before any tokenization or upstream batching to ensure raw sensitive tokens are never persisted in retrievable form.
- Per-customer no-train flag: we will associate a per-tenant metadata flag (no_train = true) that disables forwarding of any request/responses to model-improvement pipelines, telemetry aggregation, or offline training stores.
- Evidence & logs: we can produce weekly retention/export logs (hashes of request IDs, redaction decisions, and redaction rule versions) and a signed attestation from our security team describing pipeline placement and controls.
- Subprocessors: full list with access scopes — we can provide a CSV and a SOC2 mapping.

Practical notes:
- Hosted vs Dedicated: for Hosted customers the no_train flag disables model-improvement feeds and marks data as ineligible for batching that surfaces to training stores. For Dedicated (reserved) instances we can restrict access to the customer’s pool and operate in a private tenant mode; still recommend the same redaction preprocessor to avoid accidental capture by logs or observability traces.
- Prompt/response ownership: we recommend contract language that clarifies customer retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs and that Redwood will not use those artifacts for model improvement if no_train is asserted.

Next steps we propose:
1) We’ll draft a focused DPA amendment (no-train + redaction + evidence).
2) Provide a sample evidence package (audit extract, subprocessor CSV, weekly redaction log template).
3) Run a short technical call with your engineering team to validate redaction behavior (we can demo on a staging tenant).

Timeline: draft amendment + evidence bundle by EOD Monday (2027-05-17); technical call the following week if that works.

Attached: redwood-redaction-approach.pdf

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sensitive-field redaction + contractual no-train — initial questions

Sofia — quick internal notes on implementation risk and what we should include in the evidence bundle.

On enforcement across products:
- We need a cross-cutting "no_train" enforcement at the routing layer so any future telemetry or feature that introduces offline collectors respects the flag. Suggest: immutable tenant metadata stored in the control plane that routing and telemetry services consult.
- KV cache / prefix cache: ensure we do not materialize unredacted prefixes into shared caches; if any prefix caching is used, materialized keys must be redaction-aware.

Evidence artifacts to prepare:
- Redaction decision log (CSV) with columns: timestamp, request_id, redaction_rule_id, fields_removed (redacted_field_names), agent_version, route
- Access log extract for the specific customer (time-bounded) with HMACed request ids — enough for legal to trace without exposing raw content
- Signed attestation from Security + snapshot of subprocessor inventory with access scopes (read-only for observability vs write for model-improvement)

Contract language note: include a definitive definition of "Model Improvement" (examples + explicit exclusions for standard telemetry like latency metrics). Also include a cross-reference to the evidence deliverable and a timeline for Redwood to deliver artifacts after a written request (we usually propose 10 business days).

LMK if you'd like me to author the evidence CSV templates and the enforcement checklist.

—Karthik
VP, Product (Serving Runtime)
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medsys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Privacy Team <privacy@medsys.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sensitive-field redaction + contractual no-train — initial questions

Sofia / Karthik — thanks, this is the right level of detail. A few follow-ups before legal will review a draft amendment:

1) Can you provide example DPA language that specifically:
   - defines the redaction requirement and the perimeter it applies to (ingestion, logs, observability)
   - states that data subject to the redaction + no_train flag will not be used for model training or model evaluation without explicit written consent
   - confirms that prompt/response ownership remains with MedSys and that Redwood assigns no derivative rights to outputs

2) Please confirm the deliverables we can expect in the evidence bundle (CSV + attestation + subprocessor list) and the format (machine-readable preferred).

3) Timeline: legal needs the amendment draft this week and a signed attestation within 2 weeks of contract execution.

Also: our security team will want a brief discovery call to see a redaction demo. Can you suggest times next week?

Best,
Elena

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medsys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sensitive-field redaction + contractual no-train — initial questions

Elena — attaching the draf t amendment and a proposed evidence checklist. Below are the principal contract bullets we included; the attached .docx has both side-by-side redlines for your counsel.

Proposed amendment excerpts (highlight):
- Definition: "Model Improvement" means the use of Customer Data to enhance, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise alter the weights, parameters, or performance characteristics of any machine learning model owned or operated by Redwood, including but not limited to supervised training, unsupervised training, reinforcement updates, and evaluation sets derived from raw Customer Data.
- No-Train Commitment: Redwood will not use Customer Data associated with Customer tenant ID [MEDSYS-XXXXX] for Model Improvement unless Customer provides prior written consent that specifically identifies the data scope and purpose. This includes prompts, user-submitted content, and model-generated outputs.
- Redaction & Scope: Customer will provide a redaction specification (e.g., PII fields). Redwood will perform configurable pre-ingestion redaction for all requests that target Customer tenant ID [MEDSYS-XXXXX], and will apply the same redaction rules to any persisted diagnostics, logs, or observability traces.
- Evidence & Delivery: Upon a written request, Redwood will deliver a machine-readable evidence bundle containing: (a) redaction decision log (CSV), (b) access log extract (HMACed request ids), (c) signed attestation from Redwood Security, and (d) current subprocessor inventory with access scopes. Redwood will deliver these artifacts within ten (10) business days of a valid request unless otherwise agreed.
- Ownership: Customer retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs; Redwood assigns no derivative rights to Customer Data or Outputs in the absence of explicit grant.

Attachments: dpa-amendment-draft.docx (redline + clean), evidence-checklist.txt

Next steps:
- We can schedule a 30-minute demo for your security team on Wednesday 2027-05-19 between 10:00–13:00 PT. Please confirm a slot.
- If legal is comfortable with the draft, we can put the amendment into DocuSign and aim for signatures within your requested window.

If you want Karthik to add the enforcement checklist to the evidence bundle, he’ll prepare the CSV templates by EOD Tuesday.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
